title: [3.13] gh-151295: Fix use-after-free in bytes.join()/bytearray.join() via re-entrant __buffer__ (GH-151296) (GH-151306)
consumer: Objects/obmalloc.c (the freed block's pool); see the C-model sibling
live_proof: measured 2026-10-29 on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (--with-address-sanitizer, gcc 15.2, p13) with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0: ASAN:heap-use-after-free in a 328-byte region. Running the trigger is the proof. Case 28's trigger reported its recorded 328-byte heap-use-after-free in the same build.
fidelity: interpreter-trigger, real allocator. The body of upstream's regression test BaseBytesTest.test_join_concurrent_buffer_mutation (Lib/test/test_bytes.py at the fix), run for bytes and bytearray, with unittest's subTest and asserts written as plain code, driven through the real CPython. The SAME defect exists in ../pymalloc-repros as a C model consumer against the same allocator; that one locates the faulting instruction with a labelled probe and this one does not, so for attribution the C model is the stronger of the two. This one exists so the defect is also measured where it lives, in the whole interpreter.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: live and its layer measured on the host (2026-10-29); the Capstone and CheriBSD arms have not run on it
layer_note: measured 2026-10-29: ASan reported a 328-byte region, at or under the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD, and the heap report does not survive PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc on a second 3.13.7 build with ASan and pymalloc both on (CFLAGS/LDFLAGS -fsanitize=address, because configure's --with-address-sanitizer forces pymalloc off): under PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc the run dies with SEGV at address 0x8 in Py_TYPE (_PyObject_GET_WEAKREFS_LISTPTR): the stale read returns the free-list link pymalloc writes inside the freed block
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-29-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-use-after-free (READ 4) at Py_INCREF Include/object.h:824 | _Py_NewRef Include/object.h:1058 | slot_bf_getbuffer Objects/typeobject.c:9973. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
